article.title: Why Revenue Growth Can Hide a Customer Retention Problem
article.author: OpenAI learning editor
article.why: 學會拆解 revenue growth、retention、churn、cohort 與 customer lifetime value。

paragraphs.en:
Revenue growth is usually treated as a positive signal. A company that reports higher sales appears to be attracting more demand, gaining market share, or charging better prices. Yet revenue can rise even while the relationship with existing customers is weakening. If managers look only at the top line, they may miss an emerging retention problem.

Imagine a subscription business with 10,000 customers at the start of the year. During the year, 2,000 customers leave, but the company acquires 3,000 new customers and raises prices by 10 percent. Total revenue may still grow. The headline looks healthy, but losing one fifth of the original customer base is a serious warning. New sales and higher prices are masking churn.

This is why retention should be analyzed separately from acquisition. A useful approach is cohort analysis. Customers who started in the same month or quarter are grouped together, and analysts track how many remain and how much they spend over time. If newer cohorts leave faster than older ones, the business may have a product, onboarding, service, or pricing problem even if total revenue continues to rise.

Revenue retention metrics can add another view. Gross revenue retention asks how much revenue from an existing customer group remains after cancellations and downgrades, before counting expansion. Net revenue retention also includes upgrades and cross-selling. A company may have strong net retention because a small set of customers is expanding rapidly while many smaller customers are leaving. That pattern can still create concentration and product-market risks.

Managers should also separate voluntary and involuntary churn. Some customers actively decide to leave because the product no longer creates enough value. Others disappear because a credit card expires, a procurement process changes, or a contract is not renewed on time. The remedies are different. Product improvement will not fix a billing failure, and payment reminders will not fix weak product value.

Price increases require special attention. Raising prices can lift revenue immediately, but it can also change customer behavior with a delay. Some customers accept the new price until their next budget cycle, then reduce usage or switch suppliers. Looking only at the quarter of the price increase can therefore overstate the long-term benefit.

A good retention review connects customer behavior with economics. Which segments are leaving? What was their gross margin? How much did it cost to acquire them? How quickly can sales replace the lost revenue? A company that constantly replaces departing customers with expensive new acquisition may grow revenue while destroying value.

The central lesson is that growth is a flow, while retention reveals the strength of the installed base. Healthy businesses usually need both. Management should not ask only, “Did revenue grow?” It should also ask, “Did the customers we already had continue to choose us?” When those answers move in different directions, the second question often explains what the first one is hiding.

Retention analysis should also be connected to customer lifetime value. A segment with high churn may still be attractive if acquisition is cheap and customers generate strong margins quickly, while a segment with low churn can be unattractive if support costs are excessive. The point is not to maximize retention at any cost. It is to understand whether customers stay because the product continues to create enough value relative to alternatives.

Leading indicators can help before churn appears in revenue. Falling login frequency, lower feature adoption, fewer active users inside an account, more support complaints, or delayed renewal discussions may signal weakening engagement. These signals should not be treated as proof that a customer will leave, but they can identify accounts that deserve attention.

Finally, managers should avoid averaging away important differences. Enterprise and small-business customers may have very different renewal cycles, reasons for leaving, and economics. A stable company-wide retention rate can hide deterioration in one strategically important segment. Segment-level trends often provide the earliest warning.
paragraphs.zh: 營收成長通常是好消息，但也可能掩蓋既有客戶正在流失。訂閱型企業即使一年流失 2,000 名舊客，只要新取得 3,000 名客戶並漲價，總營收仍可能成長。這就是為什麼 acquisition 與 retention 要分開看。Cohort analysis 可以追蹤同一批客戶隨時間留下多少、花多少；gross revenue retention 只看原有收入保留多少，net revenue retention 再加入升級與 cross-sell。還要區分 voluntary churn 與付款失敗等 involuntary churn，因為改善方法不同。漲價也可能短期推升收入、但延後造成解約。分析 retention 時應結合 gross margin、acquisition cost、customer lifetime value 與 segment 差異，同時觀察登入頻率、功能使用率、support complaints 等 leading indicators。真正健康的成長不只是新收入流入，而是既有客戶仍持續選擇你。
paragraphs.ja: 売上成長は良いニュースに見えますが、既存顧客の離脱を隠すことがあります。サブスクリプション企業では、既存客が大量にchurnしても、新規獲得と値上げで総売上が増える場合があります。そのためacquisitionとretentionを分けて見ます。Cohort analysisでは同じ時期に加入した顧客がどれだけ残り、いくら使っているかを追います。Gross revenue retentionは解約・downgrade後に既存売上がどれだけ残るか、net revenue retentionはupgradeやcross-sellも含めます。Voluntary churnと支払失敗などのinvoluntary churnは原因が異なるため対策も分けます。値上げは短期売上を押し上げても後から解約を増やす可能性があります。Retentionはgross margin、acquisition cost、customer lifetime value、segment別の動きと合わせて評価し、login frequencyやfeature adoptionなどのleading indicatorも確認します。
